solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Calm and able to move fast when doubt's repressed

indicators.note: something repressed is held down inside, so one piece is kept within the other

parts.note: pacy describes someone quick on their feet
an if is a doubt or condition, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: Someone stays calm and stays quick once uncertainty is pushed down.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify is to soothe or quieten, a straight verb synonym of calm.

clue.text: No longer able to run in the morning over island? Here's some meat!

parts.note: being past it means being too old to do something any more
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a.m. stands for ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: An old runner who can no longer manage a dawn jog across an island settles for a sandwich instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a link in this down clue, the pieces simply follow on.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is a seasoned smoked beef, so it is one kind of meat.

clue.text: A difficult task to modify having to incorporate lines (eastern)

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take into the body, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to change something is to modify it
L is an abbreviation for line, so two lines give two of them

explanation.surface: Trying to alter something that must include some eastern railway lines is hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: A challenge is a demanding task that tests one's ability.

clue.text: Moderately good promotional exhibition

definitions.meaning: ... work is acceptable but not excellent
a trade ... is a show where businesses promote their goods

explanation.definitionFit: Fair is both a middling grade and a trade show where firms display wares.

clue.text: Learn by accident maybe contents of cover he arranged

indicators.note: the contents sit inside the container, so the letters are taken from within the clue words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone picks up gossip while reading what a cover he put together contained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' is a link word saying the definition is loose; the letters run across 'cover he arranged', dropping only the outer C and the final 'anged'.
explanation.definitionFit: To overhear is to catch words not meant for you, which is learning something by chance.

clue.text: Sadly, real CV is instinctive

indicators.note: something done sadly goes badly wrong, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A job applicant's genuine résumé, sadly, reflects only gut feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A visceral reaction comes from the gut rather than reason, so it is instinctive.

clue.text: Native of Africa could become richer soon

indicators.note: letters that could become something else are reshaped into a new word

explanation.surface: Someone born in Africa may soon be wealthier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native of Africa' suggests a person; it is an animal found there.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhinoceros is a large horned animal found wild in Africa, so it is native there.

clue.text: Equally balanced over time in long jump, say

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written over another comes above it

parts.note: even means level, with neither side ahead

explanation.surface: A long jump contest stays level as time runs out.
explanation.definitionFit: The long jump is one example of an athletic event, hence the 'say'.

clue.text: Blush when looking up earned derision to some extent

indicators.note: in a down clue looking up means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards
only part of the clue words is used, so the letters are found within them

explanation.surface: Someone goes red on being mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link; the letters NEDDER run across 'earned derision' and read upwards they give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To redden is to go red in the face, which is what blushing means.

clue.text: Political meeting — Republican supporter is there

parts.note: R stands for Republican in US politics
an ally is one who backs you

explanation.surface: A Republican backer turns up at a campaign gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A rally is a large public meeting held to support a cause or candidate.

clue.text: Nats aim, after turmoil, to find energy to go on

indicators.note: letters that have been through turmoil are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: Nationalists, having aimed after a period of upheaval, try to find the strength to continue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nats' is British slang for nationalists, such as the Scottish National Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is staying power, the reserve of energy that lets one keep going.

clue.text: In recession mines stop regular payment

indicators.note: receding means going backwards, so the word for mines is read in reverse

parts.note: pits are coal mines
to end is to stop

explanation.surface: During an economic downturn the collieries shut and a regular wage ceases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In recession' looks economic but turns PITS back to STIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed regular salary, especially one paid to a clergyman.

clue.text: Playing part as Romeo? Bravo!

parts.note: R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ole is a Spanish cry of approval, like bravo

explanation.surface: An actor playing Romeo gets applause from the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: Bravo is also a NATO alphabet word (B), which tempts; here it is the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: A role is the part an actor plays on stage.

clue.text: Flier unhappy with liquid container

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling sad
a bottle holds liquids

explanation.surface: A sad pilot clutching a bottle of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluebottle is a large fly, and anything that flies is a flier.

clue.text: Test afresh, allow men to be included: it resolves the matter

indicators.note: making something afresh means starting again, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to let is to allow

explanation.surface: Retesting while letting men join in finally settles the dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be included' says LET and MEN are part of the pool that 'afresh' rearranges with TEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A settlement is an agreement that ends a dispute, so it resolves the matter.

clue.text: Way to behave in large house, we're told

indicators.note: what we are told is heard rather than read, so a word is given by how it sounds

parts.note: a manor is a country house with an estate

explanation.surface: A guide to proper conduct in a stately home, as people say.
explanation.definitionFit: Manner is the way one behaves towards others, one's bearing.

clue.text: Look at dry English official publication

parts.note: to gaze is to look steadily
TT means teetotal, someone who stays off alcohol

explanation.surface: Scanning a dull English government document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' suggests dull or arid; in crosswords it means not drinking, TT.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazette is an official journal, such as the London Gazette that prints government notices.

clue.text: Health worker seeing believer receiving rebuke

indicators.note: receiving something is taking it in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a theist believes in God
a rap is a sharp reprimand, as in a rap on the knuckles

explanation.surface: A nurse sees someone devout getting told off.
explanation.definitionFit: A therapist treats patients for physical or mental conditions, a kind of health worker.

clue.text: Abandon black colour? No, it's fantastic!

parts.note: jet is a deep glossy black

indicators.note: something fantastic is wild and fanciful, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone rejects a black paint, then changes their mind and loves it.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw away or discard, so it means abandon.

clue.text: Opts to change hotel employee, strike results

indicators.note: letters that change are rearranged into another order

parts.note: a page is a boy who runs errands in a hotel

explanation.surface: A hotel worker chooses new options and industrial action follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage is a halt in work, which is what a strike brings about.

clue.text: British pop band of the 60s were better than the French

parts.note: to beat a rival is to do better than them
les is a French word for the in the plural

explanation.surface: A claim that a famous British group outshone their French counterparts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles were the Liverpool group that dominated pop music in the 1960s.

clue.text: A lot of people accepting Nebraska is free of deceit

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a host is a great crowd, as in a host of fans
NE is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Nebraska

explanation.surface: A crowd welcomes someone from Nebraska, a state of people without guile.
explanation.definitionFit: An honest person tells the truth and does not deceive, so the two mean the same.

clue.text: Disorganised in Agra, got disheartened?

indicators.note: something disorganised is jumbled up, so the letters are put in a new order
taking the heart from a word leaves only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A traveller in Agra loses heart because everything is in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a picture of a ragtag state.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtag means untidy and disorganised, like a ragtag army.

clue.text: Show disapproval of the unfinished compartment for voting

parts.note: to boo is to jeer in disapproval

indicators.note: an unfinished word lacks its final letter, so the last one is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone jeers at an incomplete polling station.
explanation.definitionFit: A booth is a small enclosed space, such as the voting booth in a polling station.

clue.text: Strangely obstinate man finally endorsing no candidate

indicators.note: doing something strangely means doing it oddly, so the letters are set out in an odd order
finally points to the last letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: A stubborn chap at the end refuses to back anyone in the vote.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstention is a decision not to vote for any of those standing.

clue.text: Fishing net in river

definitions.meaning: a large net hung vertically in the water

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a large hanging net for fish and the river through Paris.

clue.text: Pram recycled into aircraft steps?

indicators.note: recycled material is broken up and made into something new, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old baby carriage is turned into stairs for boarding a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as a specific example: a ramp is one kind of slope used at airports.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramp is the mobile staircase or sloping way that passengers use to board a plane.

clue.text: What's normally expected to include one (or two?)

indicators.note: including something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: par is the normal or expected standard, as in golf
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A question about what is usual, and whether it covers one or two people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link; the bracket hides that 'two' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is a set of two things, so two describes it.

clue.text: They work hard in Thailand alongside fuel tankers

parts.note: T is the international vehicle code for Thailand
oilers are ships that carry fuel oil

explanation.surface: Labourers in Thailand work beside ships carrying oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Toilers are people who labour long and hard, which matches the definition's workers.

clue.text: Empress finds artisan in revolt

indicators.note: something in revolt is overturned, so the letters are turned out of order

explanation.surface: A Russian empress discovers a craftsman is rising against her.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was the wife of a tsar or a female ruler of Russia, an empress.

clue.text: Phonily grin and get initially eager word of welcome

indicators.note: doing something phonily means in a fake way, so the letters are made into something false
initially points to the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone smiles falsely and seems keen as they say hello.
explanation.definitionFit: A greeting is something said on meeting someone, such as hello.

clue.text: Squirm seeing legal document he's appended

indicators.note: something appended is added at the end, so this piece follows the first

parts.note: a writ is a written court order
he, with the 's meaning 'is', gives these two letters

explanation.surface: Someone wriggles uncomfortably on seeing a court order with his name attached.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist the body about, as in squirming in pain or discomfort.
